struct.name: MD_SLOTID_USTAT
struct.from: census: 2 sites, 2 routines (r); census: 2 sites, 2 routines (r, indexed)
struct.doc: Layout of the slot identity and status register. The header also defines an SN00 slot bit at bit 7 and a PIMM field at 7:4. Both overlap bits named here, so they are left out. The header also defines bit 7 as the slot ID on the Origin 200 (MSU_SN00_SLOTID_MASK 0x80) and bits 7:4 as a power-supply field (MSU_PIMM_PSC_MASK); those overlay the bits above on that product and are not separate fields.

struct.name: MD_UREG1_4
struct.doc: Microcontroller and UART 1 register 4 of 16; the census has register 0. The header gives no access type, so rw is assumed. The IRIX kernel's LED macro gives it a second role: on the Origin 200 (the SN00 variant) it is the eight-bit LED of the processor in slice 1, as register 0 is the LED of slice 0, at a spacing of four registers per slice. Other Hub variants use the separate LED registers.

struct.name: MD_MIG_CANDIDATE_FORMAT
struct.from: public Linux SN0 Hub memory/directory header: MD_MIG_CANDIDATE masks
struct.doc: Layout of the page migration candidate. The header's initiator and node-number masks overlap at bits 28:20, so only the single-bit fields are imported here. The shipped IRIX kernel reads only the read-to-clear alias (md_mig_candidate_clr), in a loop until the valid bit is clear, and takes the node and page fields below from it. That a read consumes the candidate is inferred from the register name and the loop. Nothing in the kernel accesses the candidate register itself, which sits one doubleword below the alias.
